proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(d=\mu_1-\mu_0\). Positive definiteness of \(\Gamma\) implies that \(\Gamma^{-1}\) exists. The assumed strict inequality \(\rho>0\) permits division by \(\rho\). Direct calculation from the two Gaussian laws gives
\[
 T\sim N(-\rho/2,1)\quad\text{under }P_0,
 \qquad
 T\sim N(\rho/2,1)\quad\text{under }P_1,
 \tag{1}
\]
because
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P_\ell}(T)
 =\rho^{-2}d^{\top}\Gamma^{-1}\Gamma\Gamma^{-1}d=1,
\]
and the likelihood ratio is
\[
 \frac{dP_1}{dP_0}(X^{\mathrm{sc}})
 =\exp\!\left\{d^{\top}\Gamma^{-1}
 \left(X^{\mathrm{sc}}-\frac{\mu_0+\mu_1}{2}\right)\right\}
 =\exp(\rho T).
 \tag{2}
\]

We first prove the testing inequality needed for the lower bound. Set
\[
 t_0=-\rho/2+z_{1-\alpha},
 \qquad
 D^*=\{T>t_0\}.
\]
Equation (1) and the definition \(z_{1-\alpha}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha)\) give
\[
 P_0(D^*)=\alpha,
 \qquad
 P_1(D^*)=1-\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)
 =\Phi(\rho-z_{1-\alpha}).
 \tag{3}
\]
Let \(D\) be any measurable, possibly randomized event with \(P_0(D)\leq\alpha\), and put \(k=\exp(\rho t_0)>0\). Let \(f_0,f_1\) be the two Gaussian densities with respect to Lebesgue measure; after adjoining state-independent randomization with law \(\nu\), the joint densities with respect to the product of Lebesgue measure and \(\nu\) are \(f_0,f_1\). By (2), \(f_1-kf_0\) is nonpositive on \((D^*)^c\) and nonnegative on \(D^*\). Hence, pointwise on the augmented observation space,
\[
 (\mathbf 1_D-\mathbf 1_{D^*})(f_1-kf_0)\leq0.
\]
Integration and \(P_0(D)\leq P_0(D^*)\) yield
\[
 P_1(D)-P_1(D^*)
 \leq k\{P_0(D)-P_0(D^*)\}\leq0.
 \tag{4}
\]

Let \(K\) satisfy the two coverage inequalities, and define
\[
 A_0=\{\tau_0\in K\},
 \qquad
 A_1=\{\tau_1\in K\},
 \qquad
 O=A_0\cap A_1.
\]
For \(D=A_1\setminus A_0\), coverage at state zero gives \(P_0(D)\leq P_0(A_0^c)\leq\alpha\), whereas coverage at state one gives
\[
 P_1(D)=P_1(A_1)-P_1(O)\geq1-\alpha-P_1(O).
\]
Combining this inequality with (3)--(4) proves
\[
 P_1(O)
 \geq1-\alpha-\Phi(\rho-z_{1-\alpha})
 =\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)-\alpha.
 \tag{5}
\]
On \(O\), the set \(K\) contains both target values, so the definition of diameter gives \(\operatorname{diam}(K)\geq\Delta\). Since diameter is nonnegative, (5) implies
\[
 \max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
 \mathbb E_{P_\ell}[\operatorname{diam}(K)]
 \geq
 \Delta\bigl[\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)-\alpha\bigr]_+.
 \tag{6}
\]

For attainment, use the displayed regions \(A_0,A_1\) and report exactly the corresponding subset of \(\{\tau_0,\tau_1\}\). Equation (1) gives \(P_0(A_0)=P_1(A_1)=1-\alpha\), so the rule is honest. The two regions have a null intersection when \(\rho\geq2z_{1-\alpha}\). When \(\rho<2z_{1-\alpha}\), their intersection has, under state zero,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_0(A_0\cap A_1)
 &=\Phi(z_{1-\alpha})-\Phi(\rho-z_{1-\alpha})\\
 &=\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)-\alpha,
\end{aligned}
 \tag{7}
\]
and the same probability under state one. The reported set has diameter \(\Delta\) precisely on this intersection and diameter zero otherwise. Thus (7) attains (6). Since \(0<\alpha<1/2\) implies \(z_{1-\alpha}>0\), the positive part vanishes exactly when \(\rho\geq2z_{1-\alpha}\).

For \(\Gamma=I_2\), \(\mu_0=(0,c)^{\top}\), and \(\mu_1=(c,0)^{\top}\), the definition of \(\rho\) gives \(\rho=(c^2+c^2)^{1/2}=\sqrt{2}c\). Finally, suppose the two states with their common observed vector \(b\) lie in \(\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}\). Every kernel honest on that entire space satisfies the two statewise coverage constraints, and its supremum risk is at least its maximum risk over the pair. Taking the infimum over full-space kernels and applying (6)--(7) gives the stated restriction lower bound.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(0<\alpha<1/2\), \(H>0\), \(B>0\), \(q\geq1\), and \(\Gamma\in\mathbb S_{++}^{Jq}\). In the score-only experiment and parameter space of Definitions \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)\) and \(\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)
 =
 \begin{cases}
 0, & J=1,\\[2mm]
 B\left(1-\dfrac{J\alpha}{J-1}\right), & J\geq2.
 \end{cases}
\]
For \(J\geq2\), an attaining data-free randomized confidence kernel reports \(\operatorname{conv}\{b_1,\ldots,b_J\}\) with probability \(1-J\alpha/(J-1)\); with the remaining probability it draws \(L\) uniformly from \(\mathcal J\) and reports \(\{b_L\}\). This result allows several zero-score labels and arbitrary positive definite shared-control covariance \(\Gamma\). The deterministic simultaneous score-screen hull
\[
 K_{\mathrm{scr}}(x,b)
 =\operatorname{conv}\left\{b_j:
 \lVert\Gamma_{jj}^{-1/2}x_j\rVert_2
 \leq k_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(\Gamma)
 \right\},
\]
with the empty hull interpreted as empty and \(k_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(\Gamma)\) the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(\max_{j\in\mathcal J}\lVert\Gamma_{jj}^{-1/2}G_j\rVert_2\) for \(G\sim N(0,\Gamma)\), is uniformly honest and has diameter at most \(B\); it is an operational comparator, not the kernel used to establish the exact minimax upper bound.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
If \(J=1\), the defining condition \(\min_j\lVert h_j\rVert_2=0\) forces \(h_1=0\), and the definition of the score-only experiment reveals \(b_1=\tau(h,b)\) without noise. The deterministic rule \(K=\{b_1\}\) has coverage one and diameter zero. Nonnegativity of diameter proves the value zero.

Now suppose \(J\geq2\), and set
\[
 p_\alpha=1-\frac{J\alpha}{J-1}.
\]
Because \(J/(J-1)\leq2\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\), one has \(0<p_\alpha<1\). Consider the data-free kernel in the statement. If \((h,b)\in\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}\), the nonempty-zero-face condition supplies at least one \(j_0\) with \(h_{j_0}=0\), and the coherence condition in the same definition gives \(b_{j_0}=\tau(h,b)\). Therefore its coverage probability is at least
\[
 p_\alpha+\frac{1-p_\alpha}{J}
 =1-\frac{J\alpha}{J-1}+\frac{\alpha}{J-1}
 =1-\alpha.
 \tag{8}
\]
The kernel is measurable: \(b\mapsto(\min_j b_j,\max_j b_j)\) and \(b\mapsto b_L\) are Borel maps, and the rule is a finite mixture of their associated interval and singleton kernels.
On the full-hull branch its diameter is \(\max_j b_j-\min_j b_j\leq B\), by the bounded-spread condition, and on the singleton branch its diameter is zero. Hence its worst-case expected diameter is at most \(p_\alpha B\). Equality is attained within the parameter space: choose a unit vector \(e\in\mathbb R^q\), any \(c\in(0,H]\), let \(h_1=0\) and \(h_k=ce\) for \(k\neq1\), and choose \(b\) with spread exactly \(B\). This point has a unique zero label, so the coherence implication is satisfied, and the kernel's expected diameter there is \(p_\alpha B\). Thus
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)\leq p_\alpha B.
 \tag{9}
\]

For the matching lower bound, fix the exactly observed grid
\[
 b_j^*=\frac{(j-1)B}{J-1},\qquad j\in\mathcal J,
 \tag{10}
\]
and a unit vector \(e\in\mathbb R^q\). For each \(j\in\mathcal J\) and \(c\in(0,H]\), define the score mean \(h^{(j,c)}\) by
\[
 h_j^{(j,c)}=0,
 \qquad
 h_k^{(j,c)}=ce\quad(k\neq j).
 \tag{11}
\]
Equations (10)--(11) define a member of \(\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}\): its maximum score norm is \(c\leq H\), its effect spread is \(B\), and its unique zero label makes the coherence implication automatic. Its target is \(b_j^*\). Let
\[
 P_j^c=N(h^{(j,c)},\Gamma),
 \qquad
 Q=N(0,\Gamma).
\]
The reference law \(Q\), paired with the nonconstant grid \(b^*\), need not belong to the parameter space; it is used only as a common dominating measure.

We record explicitly why these laws coalesce. For \(m=h^{(j,c)}\), put \(\delta_{j,c}^2=m^{\top}\Gamma^{-1}m\). Under \(Q\),
\[
 L_{j,c}(X)=\frac{dP_j^c}{dQ}(X)
 =\exp\!\left(m^{\top}\Gamma^{-1}X-\frac{\delta_{j,c}^2}{2}\right),
\]
and the normal moment-generating formula gives
\[
 \mathbb E_Q[(L_{j,c}-1)^2]=\exp(\delta_{j,c}^2)-1.
 \tag{12}
\]
Since \(m=c v_j\) for a fixed vector \(v_j\), positive definiteness of \(\Gamma\) gives \(\delta_{j,c}^2=c^2v_j^{\top}\Gamma^{-1}v_j\to0\). Define
\[
 \varepsilon_c=max_{j\in\mathcal J}
 \sup_{0\leq f\leq1}
 \left|\mathbb E_{P_j^c}f-\mathbb E_Qf\right|.
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz and (12),
\[
 \varepsilon_c
 \leq\max_{j\in\mathcal J}
 \{\exp(\delta_{j,c}^2)-1\}^{1/2}
 \longrightarrow0.
 \tag{13}
\]
The same bound holds after adjoining the state-independent randomization used by any confidence kernel, because its likelihood ratio remains \(L_{j,c}(X)\).

Let \(K\) be any kernel honest on \(\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}\), evaluated at the common observed vector \(b^*\), and let
\[
 N_K=\sum_{j=1}^J\mathbf 1\{b_j^*\in K\}.
\]
Honesty at the parameter (11) and (13) imply, for every \(j\),
\[
 Q\{b_j^*\in K\}
 \geq P_j^c\{b_j^*\in K\}-\varepsilon_c
 \geq1-\alpha-\varepsilon_c.
 \tag{14}
\]
Define \(D_K\) as the range of the grid points from (10) that lie in \(K\), with \(D_K=0\) when no grid point lies in \(K\). Then \(0\leq D_K\leq B\), \(D_K\leq\operatorname{diam}(K)\), and the equal grid spacing gives the pointwise inequality
\[
 D_K\geq\frac{B}{J-1}(N_K-1).
 \tag{15}
\]
Indeed, for \(N_K\geq1\), the largest and smallest of \(N_K\) distinct grid indices differ by at least \(N_K-1\); for \(N_K=0\), the right-hand side of (15) is negative. Summing (14) and using (15) yields
\[
 \mathbb E_QD_K
 \geq\frac{B}{J-1}\{J(1-\alpha-\varepsilon_c)-1\}
 =p_\alpha B-\frac{JB}{J-1}\varepsilon_c.
 \tag{16}
\]
Because \(0\leq D_K/B\leq1\), the definition of \(\varepsilon_c\) also gives
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_{P_j^c}D_K-\mathbb E_QD_K\right|
 \leq B\varepsilon_c.
 \tag{17}
\]
All the laws \(P_j^c\) are admissible parameter points. Hence (16)--(17) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{(h,b)\in\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}}
 \mathbb E_{h,\Gamma}[\operatorname{diam}(K)]
 &\geq \max_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbb E_{P_j^c}D_K\\
 &\geq \frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J\mathbb E_{P_j^c}D_K\\
 &\geq p_\alpha B
 -B\left(1+\frac{J}{J-1}\right)\varepsilon_c.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{18}
\]
Letting \(c\downarrow0\) in (18) and using (13) proves that every honest kernel has worst-case expected diameter at least \(p_\alpha B\). Taking the infimum over kernels and combining with (9) proves the exact value. The argument uses unique-zero faces approaching the excluded incoherent limit, so it also covers a parameter space containing multiple-zero faces and does not require diagonal \(\Gamma\).

For completeness, partition \(G\sim N(0,\Gamma)\) into its \(q\)-dimensional blocks. Every principal block \(\Gamma_{jj}\) is positive definite. The maximum \(M=\max_j\lVert\Gamma_{jj}^{-1/2}G_j\rVert_2\) has a continuous distribution: \(G\) has a Lebesgue density, and each level set \(\{\lVert\Gamma_{jj}^{-1/2}G_j\rVert_2=t\}\) has Lebesgue measure zero. Thus its displayed quantile satisfies \(\Pr\{M\leq k_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(\Gamma)\}=1-\alpha\). Under any admissible \((h,b)\), on the event
\[
 \max_j\lVert\Gamma_{jj}^{-1/2}(X_j^{\mathrm{sc}}-h_j)\rVert_2
 \leq k_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(\Gamma),
\]
every zero-score label is retained. Nonemptiness and coherence then put \(\tau(h,b)\) in the deterministic hull. Its coverage is therefore at least \(1-\alpha\), and its diameter is at most the defining spread bound \(B\). This verifies the stated operational comparison without using it for minimax attainment.
added_lemmas.justification: The theorem closes the finite-face score-only minimax problem exactly, including multiple-zero faces and arbitrary positive definite shared-control covariance.
added_lemmas.gap: The exact decision benchmark does not by itself transfer unbounded expected-diameter loss or discontinuous coverage from the finite-sample panel experiment.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supplies the sharp weak-separation benchmark and shows that the deterministic simultaneous score screen is an honest operational comparator rather than the minimax-attaining rule.

 A_0=\{T\leq-\rho/2+z_{1-\alpha}\},

 T=\frac{(\mu_1-\mu_0)^{\top}\Gamma^{-1}

proposed_statement_changes.reason: The former statement combined the exact two-law theorem with a loose general finite-face bound. The exact general result is now a separate delivered theorem, so this node is narrowed to its sharper restricted-pair content and its restriction lower bound.

proposed.justification: The theorem solves the minimal donor-switch problem exactly and remains valid under arbitrary positive definite score covariance through Mahalanobis reduction.
proposed.gap: This node is the sharp restricted-pair result; the separate exact finite-face theorem solves the full bounded-spread score-only minimax problem.
proposed.consumer: It calibrates the identity-covariance corollary and supplies sharp embedded-pair comparisons within the general donor-face experiment.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed pair statement removes the superseded loose finite-face bound and its deterministic-screen construction while preserving the exact pair theorem and restriction lower bound.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{j\in\mathcal J}I_{j,n}(\alpha))\) is the feasible simultaneous projected confidence set. On the unrestricted-effect full Gaussian face space, \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)=+\infty\). The finite repaired weak-separation benchmark observes \(b\) exactly, bounds its spread by \(B\), and satisfies \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)=0\) for \(J=1\) and \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)=B(1-J\alpha/(J-1))\) for \(J\geq2\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The former functional named the repaired frontier without recording its now-proved exact finite-face value.

proposed.comparator_claim: Argmax-winner inference motivates separating honest projection from oracle behavior, but its selection rule and estimand differ from the exact-zero donor-face model.

Expected-measure confidence-set duality is only a template here; the exact bounded-spread score-face value is proved directly without invoking its domination, product-measurability, or fixed-measure-loss machinery.
Simultaneous inference motivates the deterministic score-screen comparator, while the exact finite-face minimax value is attained by a different data-free randomized kernel.

Weak-identification subsequence methods motivate uniformity analysis but do not supply two-sided deficiency equivalence to exact observation of a continuously varying unscaled effect; the present theorem instead proves bounded uniformly equicontinuous risk transfer directly.

Conditional Gaussian inference motivates identification-robust calibration but does not remove the effect-coordinate scaling obstruction; the qualified score-only risk comparison is proved directly here.
Few-treated-group inference with many controls is distinct from inference driven by many micro observations within a fixed finite set of labels.
Time-series synthetic-control inference is distinct from exact-score donor-label uncertainty in fixed-label micro-panels.

Global two-sided asymptotic equivalence is not delivered by the panel moment assumptions and is quantitatively ruled out for the frozen fixed-noise effect experiment; only the direct qualified risk comparison is retained.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The comparator metadata must record that the exact finite-face value is proved directly and that the deterministic simultaneous screen is not the minimax-attaining construction.

prose_updates.tldr: A finite menu of prespecified donor stacks creates nonregular inference when validity is defined by an exact zero of a noisy baseline score. The panel procedures remain causal only under the explicit nonempty exact-close and shared-slope additive untreated-change conditions; zero score alone does not imply target coherence in the abstract Gaussian limit. The unrestricted-effect full Gaussian frontier is infinite. In the repaired bounded-spread score-only benchmark, \(b\) is observed exactly and only root-sample-scaled scores remain Gaussian: its exact honest expected-diameter value is zero for \(J=1\) and \(B(1-J\alpha/(J-1))\) for \(J\geq2\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\), for arbitrary positive definite shared-control covariance and including multiple-close-donor faces. A data-free randomized hull attains the value; the covariance-aware deterministic score screen remains an honest operational comparator. The two-state subproblem retains the sharper separation-dependent value \(\Delta[\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)-\alpha]_+\). Finite-sample transfer remains limited to bounded uniformly equicontinuous risk payoffs, and none of these conditional results validates the historical CMS comparison-state estimates.

project_justification.gap: Existing few-treated panel, synthetic-control, and generic post-selection methods do not determine honest expected-diameter inference when validity is an exact zero-score face and several labels may be simultaneously valid. They also do not justify replacing a consistent unscaled effect estimate by exact observation in two-sided deficiency. The remaining transfer issue is distinct from the now-solved finite Gaussian decision problem.
project_justification.niche: The CMS comparison-state workflow has finitely many candidate labels, many beneficiaries within each state, unequal sample sizes, reused controls, and uncertainty about exact transport. A causal conclusion requires an exact population equality plus a model connecting the score to untreated changes. Ranked empirical balance supplies neither, and the abstract implication from zero scores to a common effect is an additional restriction rather than an algebraic fact.
project_justification.fill: The project proves exact-close transport under the explicit shared-slope untreated-change model, gives uniformly honest simultaneous and pilot-adaptive procedures with fixed-separation oracle behavior, and proves that the full fixed-noise Gaussian frontier is infinite when effect spread is unrestricted. For the bounded-spread score-only repair it now derives the exact finite-face value \(0\) for \(J=1\) and \(B(1-J\alpha/(J-1))\) for \(J\geq2\), together with its attaining randomized kernel, arbitrary shared-control covariance, and multiple-zero faces. The two-face Mahalanobis formula remains the sharper separation-dependent restriction result, while the deterministic score screen is retained only as an honest comparator. Direct finite-sample transfer is proved only for bounded uniformly equicontinuous payoffs; unbounded-diameter and discontinuous-coverage transfer still require extra tail and boundary control.

prose_updates.related_work: The reviewed RTI material describes the CMS comparison-state workflow through ranked baseline distance, retained comparison states, claims-driven substitutions, and person-level weighting; it does not document ex ante algebraic calibration to known population totals for every score component. Hence the workflow is a motivating and falsifiable use case, not evidence that the paper's exact-close assumptions held historically. Conley and Taber and Ferman and Pinto obtain reference variation from many control groups, unlike the many-within-group, fixed-label regime here. Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu study time-series synthetic-control inference rather than exact donor-face uncertainty. Berk et al. motivate simultaneous protection; here the deterministic simultaneous score screen is kept as an operational comparator, whereas the exact bounded-spread finite-face minimax value is derived directly and attained by a data-free randomized rule. Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey study argmax-winner selection; the present exact-zero-face model is not their argmax-selection model, and neither parameter class contains the other without changing both selection and estimand. Their work motivates only the separate pilot-adaptive oracle construction. Evans, Hansen, and Stark supply an acceptance-region expected-measure template, but their duality is not invoked because the needed domination, product measurability, and reduction from fixed sigma-finite expected measure to expected diameter are not established here. Andrews and Cheng, Andrews and Mikusheva, and Nussbaum motivate weak-limit and experiment-comparison questions but do not remove the effect-coordinate scaling obstruction.
prose_updates.interpretation: The infinite full Gaussian frontier is an ill-posedness diagnosis, not a failure of simultaneous panel coverage: with unrestricted \(b\), nearly indistinguishable score faces can select effects separated by arbitrarily large amounts. Bounding the effect spread and observing \(b\) in the first-order score-only benchmark makes the problem finite. Its exact worst-case value is nevertheless positive for \(J\geq2\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\): unique-zero faces can approach an excluded incoherent common-zero limit, forcing simultaneous inclusion of a grid of candidate effects. This least-favorable collision makes the exact constant independent of \(H\) and the positive definite covariance \(\Gamma\). The attaining randomized rule is a decision-theoretic benchmark; the deterministic covariance-aware score screen is often more operational but is not used to claim minimax attainment. The two-face formula still describes the sharper gain available at a fixed positive Mahalanobis separation. For the CMS workflow, exact calibration and untreated-trend transport must be prespecified and audited; good ranked balance cannot replace either condition.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The unrestricted-effect full Gaussian benchmark has minimax expected diameter \(+\infty\). The repaired score-only bounded-spread experiment is solved exactly for every finite \(J\): the value is zero for one label and \(B(1-J\alpha/(J-1))\) for \(J\geq2\) under \(0<\alpha<1/2\). The result includes arbitrary positive definite shared-control covariance and multiple-zero faces, but its optimal kernel uses external randomization and exact observation of \(b\); the deterministic score screen is only an honest comparator. Evans--Hansen--Stark duality remains a template rather than a proof ingredient. For the panel-to-score-only step, the reduced statistic is uniformly close only in the weak topology under the stated assumptions. This suffices for bounded uniformly equicontinuous risk payoffs. Unbounded expected diameter additionally needs uniform integrability, discontinuous coverage needs boundary control, and two-sided Le Cam deficiency equivalence to exact observation of continuously varying \(b\) is false. The accepted pilot-adaptive construction and its oracle-equivalence statement are unchanged.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Uniform causal coverage and fixed-separation oracle conclusions apply only to the triangular-array panel class satisfying consistency, stable group fractions, moment and covariance regularity, a nonempty exact close set, and the shared-slope additive untreated-change condition. In the abstract Gaussian face problems, equality of the \(b_j\) values at simultaneous zero-score labels is separately imposed and is not implied by \(h_j=0\). The original unrestricted-effect full Gaussian frontier is infinite. The exact finite frontier concerns the bounded-spread score-only experiment with exactly observed \(b\), \(H>0\), \(B>0\), positive definite \(\Gamma\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\): it is zero for \(J=1\) and \(B(1-J\alpha/(J-1))\) for \(J\geq2\), including multiple-close-donor faces. The Mahalanobis theorem separately gives the sharper exact value on any fixed two-face restriction. Finite-sample transfer is limited to bounded uniformly equicontinuous payoffs; unbounded-diameter transfer without uniform integrability, discontinuous-coverage transfer without boundary control, and two-sided deficiency equivalence to exact observation are not claimed. No reviewed source establishes the exact calibration assumptions for the historical CMS estimates.
